analysis:
The PR changes documentation only. In docs/provider/cli-reference.md (runtime constants, head lines 1968-1971) the reconnect backoff source moves to CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift. Two rows are added: a backoff reset after a stable 60 s session counted from the register frame, and a 0-1 s randomized reconnect wait after close code 1012. In docs/provider/troubleshooting.md, line 140 gets the same source-path update and the date line changes. No code, permission, key-handling, encryption, attestation or authorization behavior is modified.

Relevant threat IDs are TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider WebSocket) and T-010 (availability). The reset-after-stable-session and 1012 jitter descriptions are availability and reconnect-storm documentation. They do not weaken any trust boundary. A reconnect creates a new registered socket and connection, and the documented TB-011/T-053 behavior is that grants are bound to the current connection. Nothing here claims otherwise.

I also read the rest of the cli-reference.md paths, env-var and prefix-cache text in the supplied excerpt (units 12-13). It matches the existing T-041 posture: SSD cache default-on, 30-minute TTL, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch. The App Attest worker passthrough is exactly-1 opt-in and default-off, consistent with TB-011. No unchanged claims are contradicted by the changed lines.

Unverified contract: the actual behavior of CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift (60 s stability, 1012 handling) is not in the supplied evidence, so documentation accuracy against source was not checked. This is a documentation-accuracy question, not a security finding. No threat-model update is needed.
